scenes.visual_overview: The slide depicts ec2 selection: start with the bottleneck through labeled architecture panels and a visual takeaway.

scenes.visual_synthesis: Choose using measurable requirements, explicit data persistence and tested availability, rather than treating a single service setting as proof.
scenes.narration: This slide starts EC2 architecture with measurements, not with an instance family name. Look at the upper-left compute-optimized card: CPU-bound calculations often benefit from compute-focused instances. The same card reminds us that large in-memory working sets may instead require memory-optimized instances. Move to the purple storage-optimized card, where local input and output is the constraint, or specialized accelerated instances help suitable accelerator workloads. The lower-left general-purpose card represents a balanced baseline, while the benchmark card warns against choosing by branding alone. Now inspect the right half. The workload at the center sends four callouts to compute, memory, storage and IO, and network or EBS limits. High CPU utilization is not proof that memory or network is adequate. Measure latency, throughput, IOPS, working set and EBS bandwidth under realistic traffic, then compare supported instance families. The key lesson is to identify the actual bottleneck, choose a candidate family, and validate price and performance with reproducible workload tests before scaling out a costly design.

scenes.narration: This diagram explains why a low-cost burstable EC2 instance can work for intermittent demand but disappoint under sustained load. Start at the left blue panel. Below the instance baseline, it earns CPU credits; above the baseline it spends credits. Follow the circular center illustration from earning to spending. That budget cannot fund continuous high CPU consumption indefinitely. In the upper-right panel, Standard mode can become limited after the available credits are exhausted. Unlimited mode can maintain bursts but may incur surplus CPU credit charges, depending on usage and the specific instance family. The lower-left panel tells us what to monitor: CPU credit balance, CPU utilization over time, and actual workload behavior before downsizing. The lower-right panel adds another decision. Arm-based Graviton and x86 instances can have different cost and performance characteristics, but application binaries, dependencies and deployment processes must support the chosen architecture. Test both compatibility and representative workloads. Choose burstable capacity for measured short-lived peaks, not as a substitute for sustained compute capacity.

scenes.title: EC2 lifecycle: know what survives
scenes.visual_overview: The slide depicts ec2 lifecycle: know what survives through labeled architecture panels and a visual takeaway.
visual_walkthrough: Explain reboot memory clearing while persistent EBS and instance-store data generally remain
Trace stop/start to potential new underlying host and lost instance-store data
Show hibernation writing RAM to encrypted EBS for supported instances
Explain termination behavior and EBS delete-on-termination configuration
scenes.visual_example: Validate the depicted approach against workload behavior and a representative operational or failure scenario.
scenes.visual_synthesis: Choose using measurable requirements, explicit data persistence and tested availability, rather than treating a single service setting as proof.
scenes.narration: This lifecycle diagram compares four operations side by side, so focus on what survives each transition. First, reboot restarts the guest operating system and loses volatile process state, while attached EBS volumes and instance store data normally remain on the same host. Second, stop and start is a different event. The instance can move to another underlying host, memory state is lost, EBS persists, and instance store data does not survive. The arrows between Host A and Host B illustrate this distinction. Third, hibernation is supported only with specific prerequisites. Instead of discarding memory, it saves RAM state to an appropriately sized encrypted EBS root volume, allowing a supported resume operation. It is not a universal solution for every EC2 configuration. Finally, termination removes the instance. Whether an EBS volume is also deleted depends on its delete-on-termination setting, while ephemeral instance store data is lost. For architecture, keep important application state in durable storage with deliberate retention and backup settings. Do not assume a reboot, stop or termination has the same effect on data.
